dimensions.name: Problem & algorithm orientation

evidence.note: Inspected workspace, graph/alignment file formats, counted alignment lines and node structure across both network pairs — read sizes, format, and node-name conventions.
Verified uniqueness of the reference (perfect) alignment and that its nodes exist in the graph files — deliberate inspection of the provided reference signal exploitable for NC.
Chose SANA (Simulated Annealing Network Aligner), a known published method purpose-built for S3 maximization — a domain-informed algorithm selection rather than an arbitrary heuristic.
Checked the reference alignment's Ea (topological quality) and ran SA with a fraction pinned to the reference — recognizing the NC-via-reference-overlap lever distinct from S3/topology.
Tuned NC weight vs S3 separately, showing awareness of the differing per-deliverable constraints (S3-only for DM-HS, S3+NC for y2kr-SC).

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds level 5: it read both network pairs' sizes/format/node conventions, thoroughly inspected the reference alignment (uniqueness, node existence, Ea), and selected SANA — a published S3-optimizing method — while identifying task-specific levers (reference-pinning for NC, NC-weight tuning per deliverable, topology for S3). It falls short of level 8/10 because there is no visible broad research/comparison of multiple published methods or explicit degree-distribution characterization; it committed to SANA directly. This lands at 7, between the level-5 anchor and the systematic multi-method characterization of level 8.

dimensions.name: Pipeline decomposition & thresholds as milestones

evidence.note: Loaded/used TodoWrite for milestone tracking, then wrote and compiled a verifier (verify.cpp) and scored an alignment BEFORE building the aligner — scorer-before-optimizer sequencing, a genuine ordered milestone with a numeric done-check tied to thresholds.
Aligner (sana.cpp) written/compiled only after the verifier existed, then immediately tested and measured — baseline-then-optimize milestone ordering.
Recurring TodoWrite updates across the trajectory show sustained milestone/state tracking, not just an opening plan.

y2kr-SC driven to threshold+margin and saved early, then DM-HS handled as a distinct deliverable consuming the bulk of effort — the two deliverables tracked separately with their own thresholds, and saves gated on measured scores (implicit difficulty-based budgeting).

dimensions.reasoning: The agent decomposed the work into sensibly ordered milestones — inputs understood, verifier built and validated, aligner built, baseline measured, then optimized against numeric thresholds — with the scorer deliberately built before optimization and the two deliverables tracked distinctly against their respective targets (matching anchor 8). It shows implicit effort-budgeting by difficulty (yeast settled early, fly given most of the run) but the action-only log gives no clear evidence of explicit per-milestone fallback branches or stated budgeting that anchor 10 requires, so it lands at 8.

dimensions.name: Self-scoring against the specified metrics

evidence.note: Validates format up front: checks uniqueness/injectivity in the perfect alignment (step 8) and confirms reference nodes exist in the graph files (step 10, exact name matching).

Writes an independent verifier (verify.cpp), compiles it, and runs it on the copied reference (perfect) alignment — sanity-checking that the scorer reproduces the expected NC/S3 on a known-good input.
'Check perfect alignment Ea' — explicitly inspects the S3 numerator components on the reference alignment, testing the metric implementation against ground truth.
Recurring 'save and verify' / 'verify current best' calls show the faithful scorer used as the feedback/stopping test across the optimization arc, not just once.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent built a dedicated, independent verifier and sanity-checked it against the provided reference alignment (scoring the perfect alignment, inspecting its Ea), while also validating injectivity, node-name matching, and format — matching the level-8 anchor (faithful metric implementation that is sanity-checked and used as the optimization objective/stopping test). It falls short of 10 because there is no explicit evidence of guarding against edge-set double-counting/off-by-one bugs or treating a passing local score as scrutinized-but-not-final.

dimensions.name: Score-tracking across optimization

evidence.note: Built a local S3/NC verifier and measured the reference alignment's Ea early, establishing the scoring baseline used to judge every later iteration.
Explicit threshold awareness: pinned 32%/30% to reference to reach NC>=0.30, and later commented 'hopefully d crosses 0.32' — tracking current distance to targets.
Maintains best-so-far per deliverable: saves best DM-HS, verifies y2kr-SC 'still good' while working the other, keeps only the best parallel chain and kills worse ones.
Late-horizon discipline: repeatedly reseeds new chains from the current best state and saves best from each chain, preserving progress while exploring.
Plateau detection and strategy pivots when gains stalled — killed cycling/iterate processes, switched to LNS, greedy 2-opt, double-swap moves rather than looping the same variant.

dimensions.reasoning: Across a very long optimization arc the agent continuously tracked S3/NC against the 0.32/0.55/0.30 thresholds, preserved best-so-far alignments per deliverable while exploring, and repeatedly detected plateaus (killing stalled chains, switching algorithms, reseeding from the best state) — squarely matching the level-8 anchor and reaching into level-10 territory with its 'preserve best while exploring, reseed from best' discipline. It stops short of a perfect 10 because the log shows repeated point-in-time status polling rather than explicit numeric score-progression logging, and some redundant wait/poll cycles. I place it at 9 with medium confidence given the evidence is action titles rather than full observation text.

dimensions.name: Strategy revision when thresholds aren't met

evidence.note: For y2kr-SC (NC-constrained), pivots from plain SA to reference seeding ('32% pinned to reference', '30% pin') and adds NC weight to the objective — directly targeting the lagging NC metric rather than grinding the same run.
Introduces smart moves and an NC-floor penalty, then solves/verifies y2kr-SC (step 98) and moves on — deliberate targeted change tied to the observed shortfall.

For DM-HS (S3-only) plateau, cycles through materially different topological tactics: bitset speedup for more iters, LNS, double-swap moves, greedy 2-opt, greedy replace, BFS/greedy init — abandoning approaches that don't help while keeping the SA core.

Repeatedly 'save best' and restarts chains from the latest best state, preserving accumulated gains across strategy changes; kills stalled runs (140,174,200,252,326) and reverts a failed edit (253-256).
Final stretch is largely waiting on parallel chains and saving best — more score-tracking/grinding than new adaptation, which keeps it just below a perfect 10.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent demonstrates deliberate, diagnosis-driven course correction: it treats the two deliverables' different constraint sets distinctly (reference seeding + NC weighting when NC lags on y2kr; a battery of topological search variants when S3 lags on DM-HS), abandons dead ends by killing stalled runs and reverting failed edits, and preserves accumulated gains by saving/restarting from the best state — matching the level-8 pivot behavior plus the level-10 'combine complementary signals for the two constraint sets' trait. It falls short of a clean 10 because the final phase devolves into grinding the same parallel-chain SA with long waits rather than fresh pivots, so I place it at 9; confidence is medium because the log records actions/descriptions only, so hypothesis reasoning is inferred from the tactic sequence rather than read directly.

rubric.task_read: An open-ended global network-alignment optimization task: produce two injective node mappings between PPI networks that clear specified S3 (topological) and NC (node-correctness) thresholds. The horizon is long and the difficulty is real — hitting the numeric targets likely requires researching/implementing a nontrivial alignment algorithm (e.g., seed-and-extend, IsoRank/SANA/MAGNA-style), plus building the S3/NC metrics locally since the metrics are fully specified but the grader is hidden. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily in research, self-verification, and iterative optimization; the two deliverables have different constraints (one needs NC against a provided reference), so approaches may diverge.

dimensions.name: Problem & algorithm orientation
dimensions.description: Inspecting the graph files/sizes and the reference alignment, and researching/selecting a suitable network-alignment approach before committing.
dimensions.why_it_matters: S3/NC thresholds are hard to hit with a naive mapping; the space of alignment algorithms is well-studied, and the provided reference alignment plus node-name overlap are exploitable signals. Acting blind almost guarantees thrash.

anchors.0: Starts writing a mapping with no look at graph sizes, file format, or the reference alignment; no consideration of what algorithm could work.
anchors.3: Skims one file and picks an arbitrary heuristic (e.g., degree-sort or random injective map) without weighing whether it can clear the thresholds.
anchors.5: Reads both network pairs (sizes, format, node-name conventions), inspects the reference alignment, and picks a known-reasonable approach (seed-and-extend, IsoRank, or an existing tool) with a stated rationale.
anchors.8: Systematically characterizes each pair (|V|,|E|, degree distribution, shared node names), researches concrete alignment methods and their fit to S3 vs NC, and notices task-specific levers (name-overlap for NC, topology for S3; differing constraints per deliverable) that shape the plan.
anchors.10: Deep, sustained orientation: quantifies what score a baseline achieves, identifies the exact structural signal each threshold rewards, evaluates multiple published methods against the concrete instance sizes/runtime, and derives a targeted strategy per deliverable grounded in that analysis.

dimensions.name: Pipeline decomposition & thresholds as milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the work into ordered sub-goals (parse → metric implementation → baseline alignment → optimization) each with a concrete done-check tied to the score thresholds.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Two deliverables with distinct constraints and a multi-stage pipeline mean undifferentiated 'just write the file' effort will strand the agent without knowing whether it's close.

anchors.0: One undifferentiated push; no separable stages, no per-deliverable structure.
anchors.3: Implicit ordering only; treats both alignments as one blob and has no notion of intermediate checkpoints.
anchors.5: Separates parsing, scoring, and alignment generation, and tracks the two deliverables distinctly with their respective thresholds as goals.
anchors.8: Explicit ordered milestones (parser verified → S3/NC computable → baseline score measured → optimize to threshold) each with a numeric done-criterion, sequenced sensibly (e.g., build the scorer before optimizing against it).
anchors.10: A crisp milestone hierarchy that also budgets effort across the two deliverables by difficulty (the NC-constrained yeast task vs the S3-only fly task), with fallback branches per milestone and clear gating on measured scores before advancing.

dimensions.name: Self-scoring against the specified metrics
dimensions.description: Building/using a correct local implementation of S3 and NC (and injectivity/format checks) to measure alignments before trusting them.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The grader is hidden but the metrics are fully specified. An agent that cannot compute its own S3/NC is optimizing blind and cannot know if it passed; a subtly wrong scorer is worse than none.

anchors.0: Never computes S3 or NC; submits alignments hoping they pass.
anchors.3: Eyeballs coverage or computes a rough proxy, but no faithful S3/NC implementation; no format/injectivity validation.
anchors.5: Implements S3 and NC per the spec and runs them on its alignments, plus checks injectivity, full coverage of V1, and exact node-name/format matching.
anchors.8: Faithful metric implementation that it sanity-checks (e.g., scores the reference alignment to confirm NC≈1.0 and a sensible S3, tests edge cases like the E2_aligned denominator), and uses the score as the optimization objective/stopping test.
anchors.10: Rigorously validated scorer used as a tight feedback loop: cross-checks the S3 formula against the reference, guards against off-by-one/edge-set-double-counting bugs, verifies format matches the exact spec, and treats a passing local score as necessary-but-scrutinized rather than final.

dimensions.name: Score-tracking across optimization
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of current S3/NC vs targets across iterations and detecting stalled or plateaued optimization.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Optimization can plateau below threshold; without tracking best-so-far scores the agent won't know if it's converging, stuck, or regressing across a long run.

anchors.0: No awareness of current scores or distance to thresholds; can't say whether it's improving.
anchors.3: Occasionally prints a number but no continuity — no sense of best-so-far or trend.
anchors.5: Tracks current S3/NC against each threshold and knows which deliverables still fall short.
anchors.8: Maintains best-so-far per deliverable across iterations, recognizes plateaus/regressions, and decides when an approach has stopped yielding gains rather than looping indefinitely.
anchors.10: Disciplined trajectory monitoring: logs score progression, distinguishes 'converging slowly' from 'stuck', avoids re-running variants that already failed, and preserves the best alignment while exploring — never loses the plot over a long optimization horizon.

dimensions.name: Strategy revision when thresholds aren't met
dimensions.description: Changing algorithm, parameters, or signal (topology vs name-overlap vs reference-seeding) when the current approach plateaus below target.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A first-choice method may not reach S3≥0.55/NC≥0.30; success often depends on switching or combining strategies rather than grinding the same one.

anchors.0: Keeps the same failing approach (or ships a below-threshold file) despite no progress.
anchors.3: Minor tweaks only (reruns with a different seed) without diagnosing why it fell short.
anchors.5: When stuck, tries a materially different tactic (new algorithm, added seeding, tuned objective) prompted by the observed shortfall.
anchors.8: Diagnoses the cause of the shortfall (e.g., NC low → exploit name-overlap/reference seeding; S3 low → local topological search) and pivots deliberately, keeping what worked.
anchors.10: Fluid, evidence-driven course-correction: forms hypotheses about why a metric lags, tests targeted changes, combines complementary signals for the two different constraint sets, and abandons dead ends quickly without discarding accumulated gains.
